statement: Most of the early wall-time reduction came from cutting the epochs needed to reach 75%, through the backbone, optimizer and averaging choices: the airbench96 port, Muon, Lookahead and wd ×0.5. Resizing, compile, averaging, backward truncation (whitening at 6%, group 1 at 75%, group 2 at 90%) and early 20 px trims bring the tip to E061: 5.02 s, with a population mean of ~0.7532 (40 fresh draws on seeds 33–52) and seeds 0–2 at 0.7534. The organizer's ResNet9 baseline (59.30 s) comes from forks, was never run here, and is external and unverified. The ~12x figure is indicative only. No accuracy-per-epoch booster has gained ≥0.25 pp since E016. With H4.4 refuted, the post-keep negatives are probably real effects of about −0.2 to −0.27 pp, not seed-set artefacts: E022 (wd ×0.25), E025 (harder pull), E030 (longer free runs) and E032 (late LS removal). The copied airbench scalars therefore sit near a local optimum. Muon vs SGD is now tested: E062 cost −3.0 pp, though only one untuned SGD configuration was tried (H1.2). Still untested: Muon momentum and lr on the current tip (N1.1), batch size (H5), plain EMA and LS 0.1. Coarse labels have a strong literature counter-prior (H1.8).

An airbench96-style net is far more time-efficient than ResNet9 for 75% CIFAR-100. The net has a frozen patch-whitening first conv, Dirac init, 3-conv residual groups with widths about 128/384/576, BatchNorm-GELU, Nesterov SGD (lr 9.0, wd 0.012), batch size 1024, a triangular LR schedule and alternating flip.
The airbench96-style port trained for 9 epochs with LS 0.3 and no test-time augmentation reaches a 3-seed mean accuracy of at least 0.753, with mean time at most 9.5 s on the A100-SXM4.
With 9 epochs fixed, replacing frozen patch-whitening and Dirac init with default init lowers 3-seed mean accuracy by at least 2 pp.

Muon (Newton-Schulz-orthogonalized Nesterov momentum) on the conv filters, with SGD on BatchNorm biases and the head, reaches 75% on CIFAR-100 in far fewer steps than Nesterov SGD in this recipe. E006: +0.66 pp at ~10 epochs, confounded with batch and RNG. E062: replacing Muon with SGD on the 226-step tip cost −3.0 pp at −5.6% time. Caveats: E062 tested one SGD configuration (momentum 0.85, airbench lr scaled linearly to batch 2000). Its seed spread (sd ~0.05 pp vs the usual 0.2–0.3) suggests a systematic mis-scaling may inflate the gap (N2). PR #3 reports tuned SGD beating Muon on airbench96 at 8.5 epochs, which is not refuted.

On the same backbone and the same true epoch count, Muon (lr about 0.24, momentum 0.6, batch 2000) reaches the 0.753 bar in at least 10% fewer epochs than SGD tuned at batch 2000, and its mean time is at least 5% lower.

In short CIFAR-100 runs, end-of-run averaging is a first-order lever: Lookahead/EMA gave +0.97 pp at E005, with every seed gaining. The airbench Lookahead settings (every 5 steps, cubic ramp) and LS 0.3 throughout look like a local optimum. A harder pull (E025, −0.27 pp), longer free runs (E030, −0.24 pp) and dropping LS late (E032, −0.23 pp) are probably real ~0.2 pp harms. They are no longer explained away as seed-set bias, because E057 shows rebuilds re-draw per-seed outcomes. With averaging on, the final-LR floor does not matter (E009, C0021). Recomputing BN statistics of the averaged weights adds nothing (E044, paired). Plain EMA (H1.3.5) is untested, and external data (EMA ≈ SWA ≈ Lookahead on CIFAR-100) suggest its effect is small.
On the E005 base (with Lookahead/EMA) at a fixed epoch count, LS 0.3 beats LS 0.2 (the airbench96_faster value) by at least 0.3 pp in 3-seed mean accuracy.

On the E004 base at its own epoch count (verify from the commit; time suggests 10, not 9), adding Lookahead/EMA (airbench96_faster alpha schedule, every 5 steps, final full copy) raises 3-seed mean accuracy by at least 0.2 pp and adds less than 2% to time.
Test-time augmentation is banned, so derandomized alternating flip is worth more here than in airbench94's setting and must be kept.
At 9 epochs fixed, alternating flip beats random flip by at least 0.3 pp in 3-seed mean accuracy.

At a fixed epoch count, per-epoch cost is a large lever. Levers found: compile/fusion (−14%, E004); progressive resizing (−22% E007, −2.9% E026, −3.2% E033); and backward truncation on layers that have finished learning. Those are the group-1 freeze over the last 25% (−8.8%, E028, stacked in E034), the whitening detach after 20% (−2.4%, E036) and the group-2 freeze over the last 10% (−4.4% at −0.14 pp, E046; with +0.25 epoch about −2.1% at tied accuracy, E049). Systems overhead is exhausted: GPU idle 2.8% plus non-step kernels 2.5% (E047); CUDA graphs and graph breaks were worth <1% (E015, E017, and Fable). Convs run at 200–270 TF/s, except g1.conv1 at ~0.45x, which is only 6–9% of the step (E047). Limits: truncating a layer that is still learning costs at the dial's rate or worse. Examples: stem freeze from 60% −0.56 pp (E037); intermittent stem backward at 28 px −0.48 pp (E054, implementation unverified); group-2 freeze from 85% −0.24 pp (E053, confounded); stride-2 stem −1.1 pp (E051). Folding BN in the frozen phase saves nothing (E039).
Keeping the whole training set on the GPU and doing crop and flip on the GPU, batched, removes the CPU data bottleneck that the 4-core pin creates.
Replacing the template's DataLoader pipeline with a GPU-resident dataset plus GPU augmentation, with everything else unchanged, cuts mean time by more than 30% and keeps accuracy within ±0.3 pp.

Removing kernel-launch and Python overhead speeds up each step without changing the math. Compile plus a fused optimizer gave −14% (E004). After that the step is GPU-bound: CUDA graphs gave −0.9% (E015), graph-break removal −0.5% (E017), and GPU idle is 2.8% (E047). Rebuild variance comes from autotune kernel reselection and is not removed by dropping cudagraphs (E050). One open residue: E062's SGD swap saved 0.28 s per trial, while Newton-Schulz GPU time is only ~0.18 s (0.8 ms × 226 steps). The ~0.1 s gap may be per-call overhead of the separate per-group Muon calls (N3).
On the airbench port, adding a vectorised optimizer, channels_last fp16 and a compiled forward/backward cuts mean time by at least 10% with accuracy unchanged within 0.2 pp.
Capturing the train step in a CUDA graph (compile mode reduce-overhead or max-autotune) cuts mean time by at least 3% under the 4-CPU pin.

Progressive resizing is a near-linear time dial for tile-friendly sizes (about 0.51/0.71/0.89 s per epoch at 24/28/32 px, E012). The 28 and 32 px phases carry accuracy: dropping the 28 px phase cost −0.68 pp (E018), and shrinking the 32 px tail to 20% cost −0.97 pp (E011, confounded). Early low resolution is cheap: E026 −0.15 pp, E033 0.00 pp. The 24 px bridge, however, probably carries real accuracy: E040 read −0.28 pp, and this is no longer discounted as seed bias. Removing early 20 px steps was nearly free on fresh seeds (E061: −0.02 ± 0.06 pp). Candidate mechanisms for the late-phase loss remain unseparated: (a) low resolution at peak LR; (b) a FixRes/BN shift at the final jump; (c) too little 32 px fine-tuning. H2.3.5 and the re-based H2.3.7 would discriminate them.

On the E005 recipe at a fixed epoch count, a 24→28→32 px schedule (equal thirds, global max-pool head, each resolution compiled separately with static shapes and channels_last warm-up in build, no recompiles inside train per TORCH_LOGS=recompiles) saves at least 5% of mean time and loses no more than 0.3 pp of 3-seed mean accuracy.
Hard-example selection with a cheap proxy model (backprop only the highest-loss half of each batch) cuts total time even when the proxy's cost is included.
Proxy-based top-50% loss selection on the airbench port reaches at least 0.753 with mean time at least 5% lower than the best non-filtered recipe.

Fixed, epoch-independent cost inside timed prepare+train is about 1–2% of a ~5.4–5.9 s run, now comparable to the levers being pursued (E026 −0.18 s, E027 −0.14 s), and part of it is removable. Sources: prepare (0.21 s on trial 0 vs 0.06 s on trials 1–2, E004), the first-epoch warm-up in trial 0 (~60 ms, E012), and whitening init.

Any train or eval input not warmed up in build with the exact shape, stride/layout (channels_last), dtype and requires_grad used at run time triggers a Dynamo recompile or max-autotune inside timed code.

Warming up every shape used in training in build (synthetic data only) and dropping or padding the ragged last batch cuts mean time by at least 0.3 s compared with warming up only the main batch shape. Eval stays under 5 s for B in {1, 7, 512, 1024}.

prepare() (dataset to GPU, normalization, whitening init) averages about 0.1 s per trial (0.21 s on trial 0, 0.06 s after) and can be cut by at least 0.05 s on the mean. The ways: uint8 transfer with normalization on the GPU, whitening from a small patch subset, and warming up in build (on synthetic data) whatever makes trial 0 slower.

Moving the data as uint8 with GPU normalization, computing the whitening from at most 5k images, and warming the first-call kernels and allocations used by prepare in build (synthetic tensors only) cuts the 3-trial mean prepare+train time by at least 0.05 s. The held-out mean stays within 0.1 pp; the whitening estimate changes, so the RNG trajectory re-draws.

The binding constraint is the accuracy margin on the local bar. The tip is E061 (5.02 s), with a population mean of ~0.7532 (40 fresh draws). Seeds 0–2 vary across builds with SD ~0.17 pp around the population mean (E049: 7 builds, mean 0.7535 vs population 0.7534), so E061 passes the local 0.753 bar only ~50% of the time per build. The official 40-seed 0.75 bar is safe for any candidate with a population of ≥~0.752 (E058). Passing locally with ≥80% probability needs a population of ≥~0.7545. The job is therefore buying margin with properly powered, near-time-neutral boosters, not loosening the gate. Decision rule: any keep whose effect is <0.2 pp needs ≥3 builds × 20 fresh seeds per arm (SE of the difference ≈0.055 pp), and any time claim under 1% needs per-step CUDA-event timing.

Accuracy noise has three established parts and one suspect part. (a) Rebuild: a built artifact is deterministic (E050), but every rebuild re-draws each seed's outcome. Per-seed results are uncorrelated across builds (r ≈ −0.14 to 0.12, E057), so the rebuild SD of a 20-seed mean is ≲0.06 pp; 3 builds bound it but cannot estimate it. (b) Seed and test-set noise: per-seed SD is 0.15–0.35 pp, and the seeds 0–2 mean SD across builds is ~0.17 pp. (c) Suspect seed-1 effect: in a blind recount over post-E049 builds (E049–E062, 15 runs), seed 1 was the lowest of seeds 0–2 in 9, against a base rate of 5 (p≈0.03). That is suggestive but sits uneasily with (a). It has no practical effect on the gate, because the seeds 0–2 build mean matches the population (0.7535 vs 0.7534). (d) Selection: only the kept tip's own recorded value is biased, by ~0.05 pp (E049; N6).
For builds without cudagraphs, re-running the same compiled recipe gives bit-identical per-seed accuracies and mean times within 2% of each other.

Near the tip, true epochs are a smooth dial. Pre-freeze held-out points gave ~0.44 pp per epoch at ~0.68 s per epoch (~1.5 s/pp). After the freezes, the one measurement is E059: E046 (−0.25 epoch from E049) on 20 fresh draws against E049's 60 gives ~0.77 s/pp, with a 95% CI of roughly 0.5–2 s/pp (SE of the difference ~0.077 pp on an implied Δ of ~0.15 pp). E046's 33–52 mean must be recorded in the notebook. Every price since E059 (E061's rationale, the I096 break-even, 'no tested cut beats the dial') inherits this ±2x uncertainty until N7 re-measures it.
On the airbench port, going from 8.5 to 9 epochs raises 3-seed mean accuracy by 0.2-0.5 pp and mean time by 4-8%.

Part of E005's gain comes from the LR floor: on the E004 base without EMA, decaying LR linearly to exactly 0 (airbench96_faster) instead of 0.07 of peak raises 3-seed mean accuracy by at least 0.4 pp at unchanged time.
On the E005 recipe, decaying LR to exactly 0 instead of 0.07 of peak adds at least 0.3 pp of 3-seed mean accuracy at the same epoch count. EMA and the LR decay are only partly redundant.

On the E026 tip, replacing Lookahead (fast weights reset to the average every 5 steps) with a plain EMA of weights and BN buffers on the same alpha ramp, swapped in only at the end, changes the held-out seeds 3–12 mean by at least +0.15 pp. It is refuted if the mean falls by 0.15 pp or more, which is what C0024/Switch-EMA predicts.

On the E036 tip, recompute BN running statistics for the final averaged weights: one 32 px train-mode forward over ≤5k training images, with BN momentum set so the stats reflect only those batches, inside timed train (<0.1 s). Prediction, judged on 20 seeds not used for selection (13–32) against the E036 baseline on the same seeds: the mean rises by ≥0.15 pp and the per-seed std does not increase. Refuted if the change is ≤0.

The optimizer and regularization settings copied from CIFAR-10 airbench may not be optimal for short CIFAR-100 runs. Measured on held-out seeds: wd ×0.5 helps (E016, +0.24 pp); wd ×0.25 on the SGD groups probably hurts (E022, −0.24 pp, now read as real). E013 (LS 0.2 vs 0.3), E014 (Muon lr ×1.5) and E009 (LR floor) were 'not detected at 3-seed power'. E062 makes Muon load-bearing, yet Muon momentum 0.6 has never been varied, and the Muon lr was tested once, at 3 seeds. Whether further regularizer changes (LS 0.1, jitter, ghost BN) can pay depends on whether the recipe under-fits (N1.2.1), which has never been measured.
On the E005 recipe at a fixed epoch count, at least one point of a coarse grid (lr ×0.5/×2, wd ×0.5/×2) raises 3-seed mean accuracy by at least 0.3 pp over the current setting.
Narrowing the last group from 576 to 512 channels (the airbench96_faster width) on the E005 recipe cuts mean time by at least 4% and loses no more than 0.3 pp of 3-seed mean accuracy.

With EMA on (the E005 recipe), each 0.5 epoch cut from E005's verified epoch count lowers 3-seed mean accuracy by 0.15-0.4 pp and mean time by 4.5-5.5%. At least 0.5 epoch can be cut while staying at or above 0.756.
Running the E005 recipe offline on held-out seeds 3-12 gives a mean within 0.3 pp of the seeds 0-2 mean and a per-seed std between 0.15 and 0.4 pp.

torch._dynamo.explain finds at least one graph break in the E004/E005 train step (augmentation, LR schedule, optimizer or EMA update). Removing all breaks cuts mean time by at least 3% with bit-identical accuracy.

One-time costs inside train() that build does not cover (cuDNN/allocator first use, EMA buffer creation, first optimizer step) make the first epoch at least 0.3 s slower than the mean of later epochs on the E005 recipe.
Per-epoch CUDA-event timing of the E005 recipe shows epoch 1 at least 0.3 s slower than the mean of epochs 2..N.

On the E016 recipe, cutting weight decay further, to ×0.25 of the original, on the SGD groups only (BN biases, whitening bias, head), with Muon-filter wd left at E016's value, raises 3-seed mean accuracy by at least 0.2 pp over E016 at unchanged time.

E016's gain came from the SGD groups, not the Muon filters. Starting from the tip, restoring the original wd on the Muon conv filters only keeps the held-out mean within 0.15 pp. First check in the code whether the port renormalizes filters every step as airbench94_muon does (p.data.mul_(len(p)**0.5 / p.norm())). If it does, filter wd is inert and this is settled by reading the code, with no run needed.

On the E049 tip, replace Muon on the conv filters with Nesterov SGD (lr and wd scaled for batch 2000, everything else unchanged). Prediction: the 20-seed mean on fresh seeds 33–52 (same seeds for the E049 arm) drops by at least 0.3 pp, and time falls by about 2% (the NS share in E043). If the loss is under 0.15 pp, E006's gain came from batch size or the RNG re-draw; PR #3 predicts this outcome.

Cutting Muon per-step cost on the tip cuts mean time by at least 1.5% and keeps the held-out mean within 0.15 pp. The means: reduce Newton-Schulz iterations to 3 (airbench94_muon and Hiverge both use 3; check how many the port uses). If the filters are renormalized every step, renormalize progressively less often (Hiverge: every 2 steps rising to every 17).

On the E016 recipe, adding a 20 px phase over the first ~15% of steps while keeping at least 30% of steps at 32 px (single-factor change vs E011) cuts mean time by at least 4% and loses no more than 0.25 pp of 3-seed mean accuracy.

Part of E018's accuracy loss comes from end-of-training calibration, not feature learning: the EMA weights and BN running stats average over the long 24 px phase and the single 24→32 jump. On the E018 schedule, recomputing BN stats at 32 px on at most 5k training images after the EMA swap (timed, under 0.1 s) recovers at least 0.3 pp of the held-out mean.
Size-dependent regularization helps: on the E016 recipe, using LS 0.1 during the 24/28 px phases and 0.3 at 32 px raises 3-seed mean accuracy by at least 0.2 pp at unchanged time.

Cutting FLOPs per sample through architecture trades time for accuracy at a better rate than cutting epochs. Evidence so far: E010 (576→512 in group 3, ~1.4 s/pp, about the dial); E021 (group-2 width, ~1.0 s/pp, worse); E051 (stride-2 stem conv with the current init, −1.1 pp for −5.6%, ~0.3 s/pp, much worse). E047 shows the convs run efficiently, so MAC cuts translate to time roughly linearly and buy no discount. E051 refutes only that one stem implementation (an init or BN-placement artifact is possible), not stem restructuring generally.
On the E016 recipe, narrowing group 2 from 384 to 320 channels cuts mean time by at least 5% and loses no more than 0.25 pp of 3-seed mean accuracy.

On the E036 tip, dropping the third conv in group 1 (the block that takes more time than its MAC share, per E028) cuts mean time by at least 5% and loses no more than 0.2 pp of the 20-seed unselected mean.

Profiling one 32 px batch-2000 step of the E016 recipe shows an achieved rate of at least 90 TFLOP/s, in line with airbench's 110–116 TFLOP/s. That would leave no kernel-efficiency lever worth more than 5%.

The epoch labels are off. Reading the step count from the E016 commit shows total optimizer steps of about 9.5 × (50000/2000), not 8.5 epochs. The same off-by-about-one error applies to E004/E005 (10 epochs, not 9).

A two-point trim of E016 (−0.5 and −1.0 true epochs, LR/EMA/resize schedules stretched to the step count) cuts each 0.5 epoch for 0.1–0.45 pp of 3-seed mean accuracy and ~5% time, and the −0.5 point stays at or above 0.7545.

Run offline on held-out seeds 3–12, the E016 recipe gives a 10-seed mean of at least 0.757 and between 0.05 and 0.3 pp below its seeds-0–2 mean of 0.7607 (winner's-curse offset from keep decisions made on seeds 0–2).

Local SXM4 results transfer to the PCIe judge only partly. The PCIe card has a 300 W cap, ~5% less bandwidth and the same fp16 peak, so judged absolute times should come in ~5–10% higher, while the lever ranking mostly holds. The accuracy risk on the judge is small: the judge's own build re-draws per-seed outcomes, but the rebuild SD of a 20-seed mean is ≲0.06 pp (E057), and a 40-seed mean is more stable still. For any candidate with a fresh population of ≥0.752, P(official ≥0.75) is ≥0.95.
Building the E016 max-autotune/cudagraph recipe twice in fresh processes gives per-seed accuracies that are not bit-identical in at least one seed, with a 3-seed mean shift of no more than 0.25 pp.

At a fixed number of data passes, the optimizer step count (batch size) sets accuracy independently of the epoch count. Batch 2000 has not moved since E006. Time side: E047 shows time is ~95% proportional to samples processed, so batch changes alter time only through per-step overhead (≲1–3%). Batch is therefore mainly an accuracy axis. A smaller batch is a candidate booster if its accuracy gain beats the dial; a larger batch saves at most a few percent. Signals point both ways: E045 (more early steps, +0.135 pp, ~1.7σ) and Hiverge's 1536 favour smaller batches; Muon critical-batch theory (6x larger b* at β=0.6 than at 0.95) favours larger ones.

Under Muon, the batch size can be moved without the accuracy penalty SGD would pay. Larger batches cut step count and per-step overhead and improve GPU use in the low-resolution phases. Smaller batches add steps, which may buy accuracy that is cheaper than adding epochs.

On the E036 tip at the same true epoch count, raising batch from 2000 to 2500 (SGD-group lr scaled linearly, Muon lr unchanged, all schedules, including freeze and detach points, kept as step fractions) keeps the 20-seed (13–32) mean within 0.15 pp of E036 on the same seeds and cuts mean time by at least 1.5%.

On the E061 tip, at the same true epoch count, lowering the batch from 2000 to 1600 (SGD-group lr scaled linearly, Muon lr per step unchanged, every schedule kept as a data-progress fraction, graphs recaptured) raises the mean on 3 builds × 20 fresh seeds by ≥0.12 pp against E061 on the same seeds, at ≤+2.5% time. That rate (≤~1 s/pp) would match or beat the dial.

Per-MAC cost is not uniform across layers, but the non-uniformity is memory-bound elementwise traffic on large activations, not tensor-core inefficiency. E043: fused BN/GELU/pointwise kernels are 27% of a 32 px step. E047: every conv except g1.conv1 runs at 200–270 TF/s, and g1.conv1 (0.45x) is only 6–9% of the step. Freezing a block also skips its BN/GELU backward and optimizer traffic, which is why the freezes beat their FLOP share (E028, E046: the committee counterexamples). Remaining identical-math levers are small: cheaper activations (H6.5.1, doubted by all members), BN statistics on a subset (new), and Cin padding (H6.4.2, ≤~1.5%).
Tensor-core use drops on small spatial maps: E021 cut group-2 MACs 15.5% but time only 7.8%. So the per-pixel cost at low resolution and in the late groups is higher than at 32 px in group 1.

A per-layer torch.profiler trace of one E017 step at each resolution shows the layer-weighted achieved throughput at 24 px at least 20% below that at 32 px. It also shows group 3 below 70 TFLOP/s at every resolution.

Re-running E016 (commit d360673) through ar.py from a fresh build reproduces its seeds 0–2 mean within 0.05 pp of 0.7607. That would make E016's +0.43 pp offset from the held-out mean a persistent seed×RNG-stream effect rather than a build or harness artifact.
On the E026 tip, lowering label smoothing from 0.3 to 0.1 (near Hiverge's 0.09) raises the held-out seeds 3–12 mean by at least 0.2 pp at unchanged time.

On the E061 tip, raising the Muon lr from 0.24 to 0.36 (×1.5), with everything else unchanged, raises the mean on 3 builds × 20 fresh seeds (60 draws) by at least 0.12 pp against E061 on the same seeds at unchanged time. This follows E014's +0.09 pp (3 seeds) on the higher-wd base. 0.12 pp is about what a +0.1 s top-up buys at the measured dial.
Paired single-factor test: on the E026 tip, restoring wd ×1 (from ×0.5) lowers the held-out seeds 3–12 mean by at least 0.2 pp compared with 0.7541.

The size of the final resolution jump, not the 28 px features themselves, drives E018's loss. Swapping the order of the first two phases to 28→24→32 (40/30/30 of steps at 28/24/32 px, so the 28 px phase still runs at peak LR) keeps time and pixel cost close to E017 but has a 24→32 jump like E018. This schedule loses at least 0.3 pp of the held-out mean vs E017.

Truncating the backward pass saves far more than the truncated FLOP share (H6.6), but only on layers that have finished learning. Free cases: the whitening bias after 6% (E060), and group 1 plus whitening over the last 25% (E028, E034). Group 2 over the last 10% costs about one dial-rate quantity (E046, E049). Costly cases: stem freeze from 60% (E037, −0.56 pp); from 71% (E055, −0.29 pp); conv1-only from 60% (E042, −0.21 pp); intermittent stem backward (E054, −0.48 pp, implementation unverified); group 2 from 85% (E053, −0.24 pp). Caveat: every freeze-dose test moved the anneal end together with the detach point. So E037/E055/E053 are composites of 'lost late steps' and a 'compressed group LR decay over the whole run', and they do not establish a sharp knee at 75% (N5, H2.6.6). The 75% point itself was judged 'free' on 10 seeds (E028, SE ~0.12 pp), so it may cost 0.1–0.2 pp now (N4).

On the E017 tip, stopping backprop into the whitening layer and group 1 for the last 25% of steps, with their LR annealed to 0 by that point, cuts mean time by at least 4% and loses no more than 0.2 pp of the held-out seeds 3–12 mean.

On the E017 tip, selective backprop applied only between 50% and 90% of steps (select on a 0.5× resolution forward pass, backprop the top 50% by loss, every other batch) cuts mean time by at least 4% and loses no more than 0.2 pp of the held-out mean.

Kernel efficiency depends on whether feature-map and channel sizes align with tensor-core tiles. Tile-friendly shapes (24/28/32 px → maps 23/11/5, 27/13/6, 31/15/7; channels in multiples of 128) scale with pixels/MACs. Off-grid shapes (26 px → maps 25/12/6; 320 channels) realise only about half of their predicted saving. This explains the E024 time counterexample (−2.0% vs −4.4% modelled) and E021's sublinear MAC scaling (−15.5% MACs, −7.8% time).

A per-layer torch.profiler trace of the E026 tip shows achieved conv TFLOP/s at 26 px at least 15% below the mean of 24 and 28 px for group-2/3 layers, while 20/24/28/32 px stay within 10% of one another per layer.

An early low resolution is close to free. On the E026 tip, extending the 20 px phase from 15% to 30% of steps (taken from the 24 px phase; the 28/32 px phases keep their step counts and positions) cuts mean time by at least 2.5% and loses no more than 0.15 pp of the held-out seeds 3–12 mean.

The 32 px share carries accuracy (mechanism c). On the E061 tip, move the 28→32 px switch from 70% to 65% of steps: the 28 px phase is shortened and the 32 px phase lengthened, while the step count, the group-1 freeze at 75% and all other schedules stay the same. This costs about +7.5 ms × ~11 steps ≈ +0.08 s. Prediction: the mean on 3 builds × 20 fresh seeds rises by ≥0.12 pp against E061 on the same seeds. That beats the ~0.77 s/pp dial (break-even ~0.10 pp).

Non-uniform trims beat uniform ones. On the E026 tip, saving about 0.34 s (the time of a uniform −0.5 epoch trim) by removing only 20/24 px steps (28/32 px step counts unchanged; LR and EMA schedules stretched) loses no more than 0.1 pp of the held-out seeds 3–12 mean, about half the uniform trim's −0.21 pp (E023).

The final candidate's margin is real. Run offline on fresh seeds 13–22, the recipe to be submitted (the freeze successor, or E027) gives a mean within 0.15 pp of its seeds 3–12 mean, and the pooled 20-seed mean is at least 0.753 (SE about 0.05 pp).

The triangular LR schedule (warm-up then linear decay), copied from CIFAR-10 airbench, is mis-timed relative to the resolution phases: the peak-LR window falls in the 20/24 px phases and the decay overlaps the 28/32 px phases. Re-timing the warm-up length and peak position (and the EMA start) relative to the resolution schedule raises accuracy per epoch at zero time cost.

On the E026 tip, halving the LR warm-up fraction (peak earlier, same peak value, linear decay to the same floor), with everything else unchanged, raises the held-out seeds 3–12 mean by at least 0.2 pp. Hiverge uses no warm-up at all.

Less frequent fast-weight resets help. E025 showed a harder pull hurts, so on the E026 tip, raising the Lookahead interval from every 5 to every 10 steps (alpha per update rescaled so the total pull per step is unchanged, final full copy kept) raises the held-out seeds 3–12 mean by at least 0.15 pp at unchanged time.

Two-stage label smoothing: on the E026 tip, keeping LS 0.3 for the first 85% of steps and setting it to 0 for the final 15% (where the Lookahead average forms) raises the held-out seeds 3–12 mean by at least 0.15 pp at unchanged time.

On the E026 tip, adding Hiverge-style brightness/contrast jitter on the GPU (ranges about 0.14/0.13), with everything else unchanged, raises the held-out seeds 3–12 mean by at least 0.15 pp at no more than +1% time. The prior is low because short CIFAR-100 runs are under-fitting, and extra augmentation may hurt.

On the E036 tip, using batch 3000 in the 20/24 px phases (SGD-group lr scaled linearly, Muon lr unchanged, step counts recomputed) and 2000 at 28/32 px cuts mean time by at least 2% and keeps the 20-seed (13–32) mean within 0.15 pp of E036 on the same seeds. H5.2.1 predicts the opposite, so the two form a decisive pair.

On the E027 tip, apply E028's freeze (group 1 + whitening bias frozen for the last 25% of steps, group-1 LR annealed to 0 by then) and add 0.5 true epoch (8.75 → 9.25 true epochs, ~231 steps at batch 2000; LR, EMA and resolution schedules stretched). Prediction: mean time ≤5.75 s (below E027's 5.88 s) and a held-out seeds 3–12 mean of at least 0.7540. The keep gate is held-out ≥0.7545 plus seeds 0–2 ≥0.753.

If the port trains the whitening bias for the whole run, stopping its gradient after 20% of steps removes the input-gradient of group 1's first conv and the BN/GELU backward feeding it on the 31×31 maps for the remaining steps. (Hiverge actually stops at 0.2 epoch of 7.65, ~2.6% of steps, not 20%; airbench96 stops at 3/45 epochs, 6.7%.) Prediction on the tip: mean time cut by at least 2%, with no more than 0.1 pp loss in the held-out mean.

Freeze dose: on the N_freeze_epochs recipe, moving the group-1 freeze start from 75% to 60% of steps (group-1 LR annealed to 0 by 60%) cuts mean time by at least 3% more and loses no more than 0.15 pp of the held-out mean. This would beat the epoch dial (~1.5–2.7 s/pp).

During the frozen phase, switching group-1 BN to eval mode (running stats set from a batch-stat pass at the freeze point, then folded into the conv weights) removes the per-step BN statistics passes on the 31×31 maps. Prediction: mean time cut by at least 2% beyond E028's train-mode-BN freeze, with no more than 0.15 pp held-out loss.

E028's accuracy neutrality depends on re-annealing the group-1 LR to 0 before the freeze. An abrupt freeze at 75% with the global LR schedule kept for group 1 until then loses at least 0.15 pp of the held-out mean compared with E028's annealed freeze, at equal time.

On the largest maps (the whitening output and group-1 conv1 output at 31×31, before the first pool), memory-bound kernels (the pool and its backward, elementwise ops) and/or low-efficiency convs take a much larger share of step time than their FLOPs. This explains E028's ~27% per-step saving. Group-1 BN/GELU run after the pool on 15×15 maps and are not the cost (E039).

A torch.profiler trace of one 32 px train step of the tip shows non-GEMM kernels (BN, GELU, pool, elementwise; forward plus backward) taking at least 30% of GPU time, and group 1 plus the whitening layer (forward plus backward) taking at least 35% of the step, more than group 1's ~20% share of conv MACs.

Group-1 conv1 takes the 24-channel whitening output (Cin=24, not a multiple of 32/64). Its forward, dgrad and wgrad kernels on 31×31 maps run at low tensor-core efficiency and take a share of step time far above their FLOPs. That share is the main part of what E028/E036 saved by truncating the stem backward, and it is still paid in every unfrozen step.

A torch.profiler trace of one 32 px train step of the E036 tip (full, unfrozen variant) shows group-1 conv1 (forward plus backward) achieving less than half the TFLOP/s of the group-2 convs, and taking at least 10% of step GPU time. One trace also settles H2.2.4, H6.1.1, H6.2.1 and H6.3.1.

Math-identical padding: widen the whitening conv's output from 24 to 32 channels with 8 zero filters (zero, detached bias) and zero input channels in group-1 conv1. This keeps every output identical while aligning Cin to tensor-core tiles. It cuts mean time on the E049 tip by at least 1% (conv1 forward + wgrad is ~2 ms per unfrozen step at 0.45x efficiency, E047). Accuracy stays within rebuild noise.

E037's cliff comes from freezing before the stem has trained at 32 px (a FixRes-style mismatch), not from total lost group-1 signal. On the E036 tip, starting the group-1 freeze at ~71% of steps, just after the 28→32 px switch at 70% (group-1 LR annealed to 0 by then), loses no more than 0.1 pp of the 20-seed unselected mean vs E036 on the same seeds and cuts time by ~1%. A freeze at 65% (stem never trains at 32 px) would lose at least 0.25 pp.

Staggered FreezeOut cascade: on the E036 tip, also freezing group 2 for the last ~10% of steps (group-2 LR annealed to 0 by then, output detached before group 3, BN kept in train mode, Lookahead averaging every param) cuts mean time by at least 2% and loses no more than 0.1 pp of the 20-seed unselected mean.

The 24 px bridge is dispensable. On the E036 tip, running 20/28/32 px at 40/30/30% of steps (E040's schedule) cuts mean time by at least 2% and loses no more than 0.1 pp of the 20-seed unselected mean (seeds 13–32) vs E036 measured on the same seeds in the same build session. E040's −0.28 pp was against E036's selection seeds. The earlier '−0.09 pp vs fresh seeds' compared different seed sets and is withdrawn.

Proxy-free loss-based selection: using the main net's own per-sample losses (free from the training forward) to drop the easiest samples from later epochs cuts steps at an accuracy cost no worse than a uniform step trim. Its value depends on whether steps or samples carry accuracy (H5.2). Evidence: E031~ (top-90%: −10.7% time, −0.27 pp held-out, ~2.3 s/pp vs the dial's ~1.5, edge within noise).

On the E036 tip, keeping the 95% highest-loss samples from epoch 2 onward (same mechanism as E031; freeze, detach and resolution points kept as step fractions) cuts mean time by at least 4% and loses no more than 0.1 pp of the 20-seed unselected mean vs E036 on the same seeds.

Accuracy is carried by optimizer steps on layers that are still learning, not by pixels processed. Early on, lowering resolution at a fixed step count is nearly free (E026, E033), while removing steps costs about a uniform trim (E031, E041). E045 (batch 1000 in the 20 px phase) read +0.135 pp for +0.20 s (≈1.5 s/pp, the dial's rate, ~1.7σ). Corollary, narrowed: cutting per-step cost at a fixed step count is cheap only on layers whose learning has finished (stem after 75%, whitening after 20%). It is not cheap in general: E054 (−0.48 pp), E053 (−0.24) and E051 (−1.1) cut per-step cost at a fixed step count and lost.

The opposite prediction to H5.1.3. On the E036 tip, using batch 3000 in the 20/24 px phases (fewer steps, same data passes; SGD lr scaled linearly, Muon lr unchanged) loses at least 0.15 pp of the 20-seed unselected mean vs E036 on the same seeds.

Seesaw-style late batch growth: on the E036 tip, raising the batch from 2000 to 3000 for the last ~15% of steps (in the 32 px frozen phase) while cutting LR there by √1.5 instead of following the linear decay cuts mean time by at least 1.5% and loses no more than 0.1 pp of the 20-seed unselected mean. It fails if batch 2000 is already above CIFAR-100's critical batch.

Every seed set used to keep a tip becomes biased toward it. The challengers that follow then read ~0.2 pp low on that set: after E017 (E022, E025, E030, E032), after E036 (E040, E041, E042) and after E049 (E052, E053). E038 (seeds 13–22 read 0.19 pp below 3–12 for E036) is the only direct estimate, and seed-set difficulty explains it equally well. Seeds 13–32 have now driven E044–E054 and must be retired as a held-out set. New comparisons use fresh seeds (33–52 onward), with tip and challenger on the same fresh seeds.

E040 and E041 stacked on the E036 tip (20/28/32 px at 40/0/30/30 with 12 fewer 20 px steps; absolute 28/32 px steps, detach and freeze points unchanged) cut mean time by at least 4.5%. They lose no more than 0.15 pp of the 20-seed mean (seeds 13–32) vs E036 measured on the same 20 seeds.

The rebuild spread comes from autotune/cudagraph kernel reselection, not within-build nondeterminism. (1) Running one built E036 artifact twice in the same process on seeds 0–2 gives bit-identical per-seed accuracies. (2) Building E036 with mode='max-autotune-no-cudagraphs' (or max-autotune with a persisted, pinned autotune cache) twice in fresh processes gives bit-identical per-seed accuracies, at a time cost of ≤1% vs E036. If (1) fails, nondeterministic kernels (e.g. cuDNN wgrad) are the source and pinning will not help.

Seed 1's frequent ~0.3 pp deficit (lowest of seeds 0–2 in 14 of 19 runs, E036–E054) is a seed×data-stream interaction rather than an init property. Offline on the E049 tip: holding seed 1's init fixed and redrawing only the data/augmentation RNG (10 draws) gives a mean ≥0.2 pp above seed 1's usual ~0.751. Redrawing only the init with seed 1's data stream fixed gives a mean ≤0.752. This is diagnostic only and must never be exploited by reordering RNG draws.

The 0.19 pp gap between seeds 3–12 and 13–22 is winner's curse, not seed-set difficulty. Run E027 (commit 3735f58), which no decision on 13–22 selected, offline on seeds 13–22. Its mean stays within 0.08 pp of its seeds 3–12 mean (0.7526). If it instead drops ≥0.15 pp, the gap is seed-set difficulty and post-hoc discounts must be withdrawn.

Re-measuring the epoch dial on the E049 tip: +0.25 true epoch (~237→~243 steps; resolution, LR, Lookahead, detach and both freezes kept as step fractions) raises the 20-seed mean on fresh seeds 33–52, against E049 on the same seeds, by 0.06–0.18 pp for +0.10–0.16 s, after adding the rebuild SD (H4.5.1) to the comparison SE. This puts the post-freeze dial at ~0.6–2 s/pp and sets the exchange rate for every ranking.

Decisive test for H2.6.8. On the E036 tip, a group-2 freeze over the last 10% of steps (E046's recipe) combined with a +0.25 true epoch top-up gives a mean time at least 2% below E036. Its 20-seed mean (seeds 13–32) is within 0.03 pp of, or above, E036 run on the same seeds in the same build session. E049 met both clauses nominally (−2.07%; +0.035 pp) but within noise: the SE of the difference is ~0.08 pp, the baseline came from a different build (E044 k0), and E036's own rebuild times span 5.29–5.34 s (−1.7% to −2.6%). Read it as a tie that is ~0.1 s faster, not dominance.

The memory-bound fused BN/GELU/pointwise kernels (27% of a 32 px step, E043) can be shrunk only by moving fewer bytes, because Inductor cannot fold training-mode BN into a conv epilogue. Activation branch: only mask-based activations (ReLU-like) save backward bytes, since GELU, SiLU and tanh-GELU all save the full fp16 input. ReLU's saving (−4.8%) costs 0.54 pp (E056), so the activation route closes unless erf compute, not bytes, is part of GELU's cost (N9). Remaining routes are BN statistics on a subset (H6.5.2) and split-reduction fixes (H6.5.3).

On the E036 tip, replacing GELU with ReLU in the conv groups (keeping GELU, if any, before group 1, as in Hiverge, which uses SiLU) cuts mean time by at least 3%. It loses no more than 0.15 pp of the 20-seed mean on seeds 13–32 against a same-build E036 baseline. ReLU's backward needs only a sign mask, so the fused backward reads less.

Backward truncation in any group saves about 1.5–2x that group's backward FLOP share, because a frozen block also skips its BN/GELU backward (memory-bound), its Muon/SGD update and its Lookahead traffic. This explains the committee counterexamples E028 (27% of a 32 px step saved against a ~12% FLOP share) and E046 (~10 ms per frozen group-2 step, beating every forecast). It also explains E031's time miss: per-step cost is almost entirely pixel- and step-proportional (E047: idle + non-step ≈5%), so removing steps saves time in proportion. Per-group freeze value should be estimated from profiled time, not MACs.

A torch.profiler trace of E046's group-2-frozen 32 px step against E036's group-1-frozen step shows a saving of ≥8 ms, with ≥30% of it in fused BN/GELU/pointwise kernels and a measurable drop in optimizer (Muon NS plus update) time.

The airbench96 width allocation is CIFAR-10-tuned, and the 100-way task may be capacity-limited late in the network. However, E047 shows group-3 convs run as efficiently as group 2 (220–270 TF/s), so group-3 capacity is not cheap per MAC. The airbench paper's own airbench96 puts 512 channels in group 2, not in group 3. Reallocating width is therefore expected to trade at about the dial's rate (E010: ~1.4 s/pp), not better.

On the E036 tip, widening group 3 from 512 to 640 channels (Muon lr unchanged, every graph recaptured) raises the 20-seed mean on seeds 13–32 by at least 0.15 pp against a same-build E036 baseline, for at most +2.5% time. That rate (≤~0.9 s/pp) would beat the dial. E010's 576→512 narrowing (−0.25 pp for −4.8%) is the counter-prior.

Ghost BatchNorm: on the E036 tip, computing BN statistics over 4 ghost sub-batches of 500 (a reshape inside the compiled graph, running stats unchanged in eval) raises the 20-seed mean on seeds 13–32 by at least 0.15 pp against a same-build baseline, for at most +3% time. The prior is low because E016/E022 suggest the recipe is over- rather than under-regularized.

The binding resource is optimizer steps on layers that are still learning. Time can be saved without accuracy cost only where a layer's learning has finished: the whitening bias after ~5–20%, the stem after ~75%, and group 2 not before ~90%. Steps that still update a learning layer are worth about the dial's rate wherever they sit (E037, E041, E045, E053, E054). Measuring per-group learning progress therefore predicts which freeze, detach and batch changes are free, and blind dose sweeps become unnecessary.

A layer's remaining contribution is tracked by its relative update rate (||ΔW||/||W|| per window of steps, or the gradient norm relative to its peak). Freezing a group costs ≤0.1 pp of population accuracy once that rate has fallen below a fixed fraction of its peak, and costs at about the dial's rate before that point.

One instrumented offline run of the E049 tip (seeds 33–35, real data, outside submissions/arena/) logs per-group ||ΔW||/||W|| per 5 steps for whitening bias, group 1, group 2, group 3 and head. Prediction: the curves order the known outcomes correctly. The whitening bias drops below 10% of its peak rate by ≤10% of steps; group 1 only after ~70% (consistent with E037 and E054 costing and E028 being free); group 2 only after ~88% (consistent with E053 costing and E046 being marginal). If the curves fail to separate E028 from E037, the learning-finished account is refuted as a predictor.

Rebuild noise is correlated across seeds. A rebuild therefore moves a 20-seed mean by a build component (SD ~0.08–0.2 pp), not just by per-seed noise averaged away. Every keep decision since E044 used thresholds of 0.03–0.15 pp and is under-powered unless this SD is added to the comparison SE.

Build E049 (commit 3df6233) twice in fresh processes with private inductor caches and run each build on the same fresh seeds 33–52. Prediction: the two 20-seed means differ by ≥0.08 pp, and the per-seed differences correlate positively across seeds (the mean shift exceeds per-seed SD/√20). If they differ by <0.04 pp, the 20-seed mean is build-robust and the E044–E054 decisions stand at their stated power.

The keep gate is derived from P(official 40-seed mean ≥0.75 on the judge's build) and P(local 3-seed mean ≥0.753), and is frozen (E058). Inputs: the fresh-seed population mean, SE20, SD_seed²/40, σ_build ≤0.06 pp (upper bound) and a 0.05 pp judge-drift term. The official clause is easy (σ_tot ~0.09 pp; E052 at a population of 0.7524 passed twice). The local clause binds: with a seeds 0–2 build SD of ~0.17 pp, a population of ~0.7535 passes ~50% of the time and ~0.7545 passes ~80%. So the gate does not over-price official margin, but local margin must be bought.

Run E052 (ce17ae7) and E053 (f30d362) on fresh seeds 33–52 alongside E049. Prediction: both population means are ≥0.751, and with the measured rebuild SD the computed P(official ≥0.75) is ≥0.9 for each. Their deficit vs E049 on the fresh seeds is ≤0.15 pp, smaller than the −0.21/−0.24 measured on E049's reused seeds 13–32.

Winner's curse on seeds 13–32: E049, kept on seeds 13–32 at 0.7539, reads at least 0.1 pp lower on fresh seeds 33–52 in the same build. If it reads within 0.05 pp, the post-keep ~0.2 pp challenger deficits are real effects, not baseline bias.

E054's −0.48 pp is partly an implementation artifact. In an offline unit test of the alternating stem step on synthetic data, at least one of the following fails: (a) group-1 params, grads and Muon momentum buffers are bit-unchanged across a detached step; (b) the next full step's update equals a reference that never ran the detached variant; (c) BN running stats and Lookahead state behave identically. If all three pass, E054 stands as evidence that stem learning in the 28 px phase is step-limited.

The whitening bias finishes learning far earlier than 20% of steps (Hiverge ~2.6%, airbench96 6.7%). On the E049 tip, moving the whitening detach (with its LR annealed to 0) from 20% to 6% of steps cuts mean time by 0.3–0.7% and loses no more than 0.05 pp on fresh seeds 33–52 against E049 on the same seeds. Judge time on per-step CUDA-event timing. Also verify by code read that E061 (376f231) carries the 6% detach: its description says 'on the E049 tip'.

BatchNorm statistics from a subset: on the E049 tip, compute training-BN mean/var over 1/4 of each batch (a strided slice inside the compiled graph; normalization still applied to the whole batch) in group 1 and group 2 only. This cuts mean time by ≥2% and loses ≤0.1 pp on fresh seeds 33–52. Only the forward reduction gets cheaper, so the saving is bounded by the BN-stat share of the fused 27%.

In the E049 32 px step, at least one training-BN reduction on the 31×31 or 15×15 maps compiles to a two-pass or split reduction under channels_last (visible in the Inductor output and as a kernel achieving <60% of HBM bandwidth in the E043-style trace). If none does, the fused BN share is already near its bandwidth floor and the identical-math route into H6.5 closes.

CIFAR-100's 20 coarse superclass labels, which ship with the training set, can supply extra training signal at zero per-step cost: smoothing mass placed on same-superclass classes, or an auxiliary coarse-label loss. This raises fine-label accuracy per epoch in short runs, a structural sample-efficiency gain of the kind H1 says scalar sweeps cannot reach. Precondition: RULES.md and the data loader must allow coarse labels as part of the 50k training data.

If the rules allow coarse labels: on the E049 tip, hierarchical label smoothing (LS total 0.3, with half of the smoothing mass spread over the 4 same-superclass fine classes and half uniform) raises the 20-seed mean on fresh seeds 33–52 by ≥0.15 pp against E049 on the same seeds, at unchanged time.

Fidelity check by code read: airbench96(_faster) and Hiverge both freeze the BatchNorm scale (weight.requires_grad=False). If the port trains it, freezing it on the E049 tip changes the 20-seed fresh-seed mean by no more than ±0.1 pp and cuts time by ≥0.5% (fewer SGD params, less fused backward). If the port already freezes it, close this by reading the code.

In the ~225-step regime, accuracy is set by per-step update and representation quality more than by step or pixel count. Changes that degrade per-step progress cost far above the dial: SGD in place of Muon −3.0 pp (E062), ReLU in place of GELU −0.54 pp (E056), stride-2 stem −1.1 pp (E051), each 3–10x worse than its time saving buys at ~0.77 s/pp. Changes that improve per-step quality (Muon hyperparameters, batch size, fitting speed) are the main untried path to the ~0.13 pp of margin the local bar needs.

Muon's hyperparameters are CIFAR-10 airbench94 copies (lr 0.24, momentum 0.6, 3-ish NS steps) that were never tuned for a 225-step CIFAR-100 run with progressive resizing and freezes. E014 (lr ×1.5, +0.09 pp, 3 seeds) is the only probe. Given E062, a modest retune is the most likely near-time-neutral booster.

On the E061 tip, raising the Muon momentum from 0.6 to 0.8 (Nesterov kept, lr unchanged) raises the mean on 3 builds × 20 fresh seeds by ≥0.12 pp against E061 on the same seeds at unchanged time. It is refuted if it falls by ≥0.12 pp. Muon critical-batch theory (a lower b* at higher β) and the CIFAR-100 critical-damping result (faster early, −1.7 pp final) both predict that outcome.

The recipe under-fits CIFAR-100: at the end of training, the averaged weights' training accuracy is well below saturation. Changes that speed fitting help (E016 wd ×0.5), and changes that slow fitting or reduce capacity cost heavily (E051, E056, E062). Then regularizer additions (jitter, ghost BN, extra LS) are not worth testing. The counterpoints are E022 (wd ×0.25 hurt) and E032 (removing LS late hurt), which suggest some regularization is still useful.

Diagnostic, offline and outside the timed path: on the E061 tip (seeds 33–35), evaluate the final averaged weights on a fixed 10k training subset at 32 px with no augmentation and no LS. Prediction: train top-1 ≤90% (under-fitting). If it is ≥97%, the recipe is fitting-saturated: test LS 0.1 (H1.5.5) and jitter (H1.5.8) on 60 draws, and deprioritize the optimizer and capacity work in N1.1.

E062's −3.0 pp, with near-identical seeds (sd ~0.05 pp), is largely an SGD mis-scaling artefact, not optimizer quality: the conv lr was scaled for batch 2000 on top of the port's own airbench batch normalization, and/or the filter wd was coupled to lr 9.0. Reading commit cdfccca confirms a double scaling or coupling, and a 3-seed SGD run at lr ×0.5 recovers ≥1 pp of the gap. This is low priority unless the SGD branch is reopened; even then, closing the gap to within 0.35 pp is needed for SGD to break even.

E062's time counterexample: dropping Muon saved 0.28 s per trial, but Newton-Schulz GPU time is only ~0.18 s (0.8 ms × 226, E043). The excess ~0.1 s is per-call host and launch overhead from separate per-group Muon calls (three filter groups, each with its own schedule) plus the non-fused momentum update. Merging all Muon filter groups into one compiled, batched NS-plus-update call, with GPU-resident per-group LR tables and identical math, cuts mean time on the E061 tip by ≥1% (≥0.05 s), confirmed by per-step CUDA-event timing, with per-seed accuracies unchanged within rebuild noise. It is refuted if the per-step GPU time of the Muon section already accounts for the 0.28 s (E047's 2.8% idle bounds the overhead share).

The 75% group-1 freeze is not free; E028's '−0.01 pp' was a 10-seed reading with SE ~0.12 pp. On the E061 tip, moving the group-1 freeze, and its anneal end, from 75% to 80% of steps costs about +11 steps × 7.7 ms ≈ +0.09 s and raises the mean on 3 builds × 20 fresh seeds by ≥0.12 pp against E061 on the same seeds. That beats the ~0.77 s/pp dial (break-even ~0.11 pp). If it gains ≥0.15 pp, spend it on an early 20 px trim.

Freeze-dose readings are anneal-plus-freeze composites. On the E061 tip, keep group 1's LR anneal ending at 75% but move only the detach earlier, to 71% (group 1 gets ~9 more steps at a near-zero LR before the detach, then no updates). Prediction: this loses ≤0.1 pp on 3 builds × 20 fresh seeds against E061, far less than E055's −0.29 pp for the same detach point, showing that most of E055's cost came from compressing the group-1 decay over ~23–71% of the run, not from the lost late steps.

Selection bias sits only in the kept tip's own recorded value and is about the size of the keep margin (~0.05 pp; E049: 0.7539 on 13–32 vs 0.7534 on fresh 33–52). Every rebuild re-draws per-seed outcomes (E057), so reused seed sets carry no persistent bias toward a tip. The ~0.2 pp deficits that challengers showed after each keep (E022, E025, E030, E032, E040–E042, E052, E053) are mostly real effects of those changes. Rule: re-measure the baseline in fresh builds rather than retiring seed sets.

Run the E061 tip (376f231) on reserved seeds 53–72 in 2 fresh builds (40 draws). Prediction: its mean lies within 0.06 pp of its 33–52 mean (0.7532). This also gives the confirmation read the H4.6 gate requires. A drop of ≥0.12 pp would revive a selection-bias account beyond the tip's recorded value.

Re-measure the post-freeze epoch dial at full power. On the E061 tip, run −0.25 and +0.25 true-epoch arms (all schedules kept as step fractions), each over 3 builds × 20 fresh seeds, against E061 on the same seeds. Prediction: the dial lies in 0.5–1.2 s/pp, and its 95% CI excludes 1.5 s/pp. This replaces E059's single 20-draw point as the exchange rate for every booster and cut.

Early-trim dose (the I099 crux shared by all four committee members). On the E061 tip, remove a further 12 steps from the 20 px phase (225 → 213), with the 28/32 px phases, whitening detach and freezes kept at the same absolute steps. This saves ~0.15 s and loses ≤0.1 pp on 3 builds × 20 fresh seeds against E061. At ~0.77 s/pp the break-even loss is ~0.2 pp. It is refuted, meaning E061 used up the free early steps, if the loss is ≥0.2 pp.

Part of GELU's fused-kernel cost (E056: ReLU saved 4.8%) is erf compute, not bytes. Offline profile of the E061 32 px and 28 px steps (synthetic channels_last, batch 2000): approximate='tanh' GELU cuts per-step GPU time by ≥1.5%. If it does, the change is committed only if the mean on 60 draws stays within 0.1 pp. The search predicts ~0: tanh-GELU saves the same fp16 input and moves the same bytes. A null result closes H6.5's activation branch with no accuracy run.
